## Digital Marketing Agency in Pune: What Google Search Console's New AI Visibility Reports Mean for Your Content in 2026

Google Search Console now reports on how your pages perform inside AI Overviews and AI Mode, not just classic blue-link results, and by late 2026 it has also started surfacing where your content and links show up on Instagram through Google's indexing of that platform. For a business that has spent years judging its SEO purely by "position 1-10" in a traditional results list, this changes what a digital marketing agency in Pune should actually be reporting on every month, because a page can now be doing real work for you inside an AI-generated answer while looking, on paper, like it dropped in traditional rankings. This article explains exactly what Search Console shows now, what it still can't tell you, and how to change a monthly SEO report so it reflects reality instead of a metric that quietly stopped telling the whole story.

This isn't a general "how to use Search Console" primer. It assumes you already know the Performance report. It's specific to what changed in 2026: the new AI-surface reporting, the Instagram indexing update, and what a competent agency should be doing differently in client reporting because of both.

### The core question, answered directly

If your Search Console reports still only show impressions, clicks, and average position for classic search results, you are working with an incomplete picture of your actual visibility, because a growing share of the queries your content used to win are now answered directly inside an AI Overview or AI Mode response — sometimes citing your page (which counts as a form of impression, even with no click), sometimes not citing anyone identifiable at all. Google's newer reporting surfaces some of this, but not all of it, and understanding exactly where the gap sits is what separates a useful monthly report from a misleading one.

## What Actually Changed in Search Console

Google has been rolling out dedicated reporting for AI-driven search surfaces through 2026, after testing began earlier in the year. The practical addition: Search Console's Performance report now lets you filter and see impressions and clicks specifically attributable to AI Overviews and AI Mode as distinct search types, rather than lumping every appearance into one undifferentiated "Web" search type the way it did before. This matters because AI Overviews behave completely differently from a normal result: a page can be cited inside an AI Overview and generate an impression without ever showing as a separate blue link on the same page, and previously that appearance was either invisible in reporting or blended into numbers that made it impossible to isolate.

Separately, as of mid-2026 Search Console began tracking content on Instagram as part of its Search-related surfaces. In practical terms, this means the "platforms" or "properties" view in Search Console can now show which of your queries are surfacing Instagram content — your business's own account, or others discussing you — alongside your website's own pages. This reflects a real shift on Google's side: Instagram posts and Reels are increasingly treated as indexable, searchable content that can appear directly in Google Search results, not just within Instagram's own app search. For any brand that treats Instagram purely as a paid-media and engagement channel, disconnected from its SEO strategy, that separation stopped making sense the moment Google started indexing and reporting on it in the same tool used for website SEO.

## Why This Matters More in India Than the Global Average Might Suggest

Indian search behaviour has two specific characteristics that make this change land harder here than in some other markets. First, mobile-first, app-adjacent discovery — a large share of Indian consumers research a business via Instagram and WhatsApp before or instead of a traditional Google search on desktop, so a reporting tool that finally connects Instagram visibility to the same dashboard as website SEO closes a real blind spot that agencies serving Indian SMBs have had for years. Second, AI-assisted search adoption in India has grown quickly across Gemini, ChatGPT and Google's AI Mode, particularly among younger, urban, English-and-Hindi-bilingual users doing comparison research — exactly the audience searching "digital marketing agency Pune" or "web development company in Pune" style buyer-intent queries this site targets. A digital marketing agency reporting only classic-result rankings to a Pune-based client in 2026 is measuring a shrinking slice of where that client's actual buyers are looking.

## Reading the New Reports Correctly

The AI Overviews and AI Mode data in Search Console comes with real limitations that a report presenting it needs to state plainly, not gloss over.

**Impressions without clicks are common, and that's expected, not a failure.** An AI Overview citation frequently satisfies the user's question directly in the answer, with no need to click through. A page showing rising AI-surface impressions alongside flat or falling clicks isn't necessarily losing ground — it may be doing exactly what an authoritative source is supposed to do inside an AI answer. The metric to watch isn't click-through rate in isolation; it's whether brand-name searches, direct traffic, and WhatsApp/contact-form enquiries are trending in a way consistent with more people encountering the brand through AI answers even without clicking.

**Not every AI answer citation is captured.** Search Console's AI-surface reporting reflects what Google's own AI Overviews and AI Mode show — it says nothing about how a page performs inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Gemini's standalone app, all of which pull from different crawling and indexing systems entirely (a topic covered in more technical depth in our guide to [controlling AI crawlers with robots.txt](/blog/web-development-company-pune-ai-crawlers-robots-txt-2026)). A brand can be well cited in ChatGPT answers and invisible in Google's own AI Overview reporting, or the reverse, and Search Console will only ever tell you about the Google side.

**Instagram indexing data is new and coarse.** Because Google only recently began treating Instagram content as an indexable search surface at this depth, expect the reporting here to be less mature and less granular than the decade-old Performance report for web results. Use it as a directional signal — "is our Instagram presence showing up in Google Search at all" — rather than a precise ranking dashboard yet.

### A comparison of what each report actually tells you

| Report | What it shows | What it misses |
|---|---|---|
| Classic Performance (Web) | Impressions, clicks, CTR, position for traditional blue-link results | AI Overview/AI Mode citations shown separately, non-Google AI surfaces |
| AI Overviews / AI Mode filter | Impressions and clicks specifically tied to AI-generated answers | Whether a citation without a click still influenced a later branded search or visit |
| Instagram/platform tracking | Whether your Instagram content surfaces for Google queries | Ranking position within Instagram's own in-app search; engagement metrics live in Instagram Insights, not here |
| GA4 / analytics | Actual sessions, conversions, and on-site behaviour once someone does click | Zero-click impressions and brand lift from being cited without a click |

The honest takeaway: no single dashboard gives you the full picture in 2026, and a report built entirely on one of these while ignoring the others tells a partial story either way.

## What a Monthly SEO Report Should Actually Include Now

A report that hasn't changed its structure since 2023 is very likely still leading with average position and total clicks as the headline numbers, which quietly under-represents any client whose content is winning AI Overview citations without a proportional click increase. A more honest structure for 2026 separates three things: classic search performance (impressions, clicks, position, same as always); AI-surface performance (impressions and clicks specifically filtered to AI Overviews/AI Mode, tracked as its own trend line rather than folded into the total); and cross-platform visibility (Instagram indexing signal alongside the brand's own social performance metrics, since the two are now genuinely connected in Google's own tooling). None of this requires new paid tools — it requires actually using the segmentation Search Console already provides instead of exporting the default totals view and calling it a report.

## What This Changes About Content Strategy, Not Just Reporting

Reporting differently is only useful if it changes what gets built. Two practical shifts follow directly from this data becoming visible:

**Content built to be cited, not just clicked, is now a legitimate strategy, not a consolation prize.** A clearly structured page — a direct answer in the opening paragraph, a well-labelled comparison table, explicit FAQ sections — is the kind of content AI Overviews tend to draw from and cite, and Search Console can now show you whether that's actually happening for your pages. This is consistent with technical fundamentals we've written about elsewhere: a page a crawler or an AI answering system can parse cleanly outranks a page stuffed with heavy client-side rendering and unclear headings, independent of the AI angle, and the discipline of writing to answer a question in the first two sentences (which every article on this site follows) turns out to double as the format AI Overviews prefer to cite.

**Instagram content needs to be written like it's indexable, because it now more clearly is.** A caption that's purely an image description with no useful text, or hashtag-only copy, gives Google's indexing of that content nothing to match against a real search query. A caption written the way you'd write a short, genuinely informative sentence — the kind you'd want an AI Overview or a Google Search result to be able to quote — is now doing double duty as social copy and as indexable search content, whereas before it was only ever judged on engagement inside Instagram's own algorithm.

This connects to broader shifts in how buyers now discover businesses before ever running a classic search, a trend we've also covered from the standpoint of how Google's own conversational surface reshapes SEO strategy in [what Google's AI Mode means for a digital marketing agency in Pune](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-google-ai-mode-2026), and from the local-search angle in our [local SEO and Google Map Pack guide](/blog/local-seo-google-map-pack-pune-2026), since AI Overview citations and Map Pack visibility increasingly draw on the same underlying content quality signals.

## Setting This Up Correctly: A Practical Walkthrough

For an agency or an in-house marketer doing this themselves, the actual steps are straightforward, but a few missteps are common enough to call out directly.

1. **Open the Performance report and check the Search type filter first**, not last. By default it may already include all types combined, which is exactly the blended view that hides AI-surface performance inside the total. Explicitly filter to isolate AI Overviews/AI Mode traffic where the option is available, and compare it side by side with the "Web" search type rather than reading one number that mixes both.
2. **Segment by page, not just by query**, when reviewing AI-surface data. A handful of pages — usually the ones structured with a direct-answer opening, clear headings and an FAQ section — tend to account for a disproportionate share of AI citations, and identifying which pages those are tells you what to replicate in future content, not just what happened in the past.
3. **Check the Instagram/platform data under the same property**, if your business has connected its Instagram presence to the same Search Console verification. This is easy to miss because it doesn't live inside the main Performance report the way AI Overview data does — it's a separate view, and an agency that only checks the familiar Performance tab will simply never see it.
4. **Cross-reference with GA4** for the sessions and conversions that do result from a click, since Search Console never shows what happens after someone lands on your site. The AI-surface impression data answers "were we visible"; GA4 answers "what happened when someone acted on that visibility." A report using only one of the two is incomplete in a specific, avoidable way.
5. **Set a recurring monthly export**, because Search Console's own historical data window is limited (typically around 16 months), and a business that wants a longer trend line for AI-surface visibility specifically — still a genuinely new metric as of 2026 — needs to start archiving it now rather than assuming Google will always show a full history on demand later.

None of these steps require a paid add-on. They require someone actually opening the newer views instead of exporting the same default report that's been used for years, which is, in practice, the most common reason this data goes unused even when a business already has access to it. This kind of reporting discipline is exactly what should sit inside any ongoing [SEO](/services/seo) or [social media management](/services/social-media) engagement — not a once-a-year audit, but a monthly habit of actually reading the segments a tool already gives you.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Do I need a new tool to see AI Overview performance, or is it already in Search Console?

It's already in Search Console — no new subscription or tool is required. The AI Overviews and AI Mode data appears as an additional way to segment the existing Performance report; you may need to check that you're filtering by the correct search type rather than assuming the default totals view already separates it out.

### Why does my AI-surface impressions number keep rising while clicks stay flat?

This is expected behaviour, not a bug or a sign of underperformance. AI Overviews frequently answer the user's question directly in the generated summary, which can satisfy the search without a click. Watch branded search volume, direct traffic and enquiry volume as complementary signals rather than judging AI-surface visibility purely on click-through rate.

### Does Google indexing my Instagram content mean I should abandon a separate SEO strategy for my website?

No. It means the two channels are more connected than before in Google's own tooling, not that one replaces the other. Your website remains the asset you fully control and the one your ad campaigns, contact forms and conversions ultimately depend on; Instagram indexing is an additional discovery surface, not a substitute.

### Can a small local business realistically benefit from AI Overview citations, or is this only relevant to large publishers?

Local and niche businesses are frequently well positioned here, because AI Overviews for specific, well-defined questions ("what does an NGO donation platform need for 80G compliance," for instance) often favour a page that answers the question precisely and specifically over a large generic publisher's broader coverage of the same topic. Depth and specificity, not domain size alone, is what tends to earn a citation.

### How often should we check the AI-surface data in Search Console?

Monthly is reasonable for most businesses, aligned with a normal reporting cycle, though a business publishing content aggressively to capture AI Overview citations may want to check more frequently in the weeks immediately after publishing a new piece, since AI Overview citation behaviour can shift faster than traditional ranking position does.

## Where to Start

If your last SEO report from any agency was structured exactly like a report from 2022 — total impressions, total clicks, average position, nothing more — that's worth raising with whoever produces it, because Search Console itself has moved past that structure and a report that hasn't kept up is hiding information you're already paying to have visibility into. As a digital marketing agency in Pune, we build this segmentation into every client report now: classic performance, AI-surface performance, and cross-platform visibility, tracked separately rather than blended into one misleading total.
